items.headline: Amazon and Intel earnings reignite AI-capex fears, triggering Nasdaq's worst day since June
items.summary: Amazon shares fell ~6.5% after reporting $77B of Q3 capex (vs ~$59B expected) and negative free cash flow for a second straight quarter while reaffirming ~$220B 2026 capex guidance; Intel collapsed ~29%, its worst day in decades, on weak Q4 revenue guidance ($15-16B) tied to an Israel plant shutdown and soft PC demand. The combined AI-spending-versus-returns anxiety drove the Nasdaq -2.86% and S&P 500 -1.82% on Oct 30, the worst session for both indices since June.
items.actionable: This AI-capex equity shock, not a rates story, is the proximate spark behind Friday's cross-asset liquidation hitting the leveraged silver/gold miner book, HK tech and crypto simultaneously -- expect continued correlation to Nasdaq follow-through at Monday's Asia open.

items.headline: Fed's Musalem, Logan and Daly all push for more hikes in Friday remarks
items.summary: In Friday appearances, Dallas Fed's Logan told Davidson College students the FOMC "needs to implement at least two more 25bp rate increases," adding that "skipping a meeting does not change the monetary policy destination." St. Louis Fed's Musalem said another hike "will need to happen soon" and warned that delaying tightening makes later adjustments more disruptive, while SF Fed's Daly focused her remarks on AI's bearing on the dual mandate.
items.actionable: A genuine chorus of hawkish Fed voices into the weekend confirms the rate repricing hitting gold/silver is a real policy headwind, not just Friday's equity panic -- a structural, not transient, risk for the 2x leveraged metals sleeve.

items.headline: December hike odds slip to ~69-72% from ~80% even as Fed speakers turn more hawkish
items.summary: CME FedWatch-style odds of a December 9 rate hike fell from roughly 79.9% on Oct 29 to about 72.4% intraday and ~69.4% by the Oct 30 close, even as Musalem, Logan and Daly all leaned hawkish. The drag came from Friday's tech-driven equity selloff and a softer-than-feared Q3 Employment Cost Index (wages +0.7% vs +0.9% prior).
items.actionable: Odds easing despite hawkish Fedspeak shows markets reading Friday's stock rout as growth-negative -- if that framing holds into next week it could cap further downside in gold even as the metals trade through the immediate margin-call liquidation.

items.headline: Gold craters to ~$3,897 and silver breaks below $50 as liquidation selling overwhelms metals
items.summary: Gold spot fell 3.1% to $3,897.48/oz and silver dropped 5.9% to $49.09/oz on Oct 30, with both metals breaking through levels that had held for months. Analysts attributed the move to a mix of hawkish Fed repricing and correlated liquidity-driven selling, as investors facing margin calls from the tech-stock rout dumped their most liquid winners -- gold and silver futures -- first.
items.actionable: This looks like a liquidity/margin-driven air pocket layered on top of a genuine hawkish-Fed repricing -- real risk of further forced deleveraging in the 2x leveraged metals position before any bounce, so size any add with that two-part cause in mind.

items.headline: MP Materials falls 6% and rare-earth peers slide as the same margin-call liquidation hits the sector
items.summary: MP Materials dropped 6% to around $38.49-$39.46 intraday on Oct 30, amplified by the Nasdaq's ~4% tech-driven selloff, days after Goldman Sachs cut its price target to $57 from $65. The rare-earth/critical-minerals complex broadly sold off alongside gold/silver miners as the same forced-liquidation dynamic -- selling the most liquid, highest-conviction positions to raise cash -- spread across leveraged portfolios.
items.actionable: Goldman's price-target cut plus the correlated liquidity shock is a read-through to lower near-term conviction across the whole rare-earth watchlist (MP, Energy Fuels) -- treat Friday's drop as forced-selling noise rather than a thesis change, pending confirmation at Nov 4-5 earnings.

items.headline: China's Nov 10 rare-earth truce deadline still has no matching legal text from Beijing
items.summary: Washington says the US-China rare-earth export-control truce has been extended to Jan 10, 2027, but as of Oct 30 China's Ministry of Commerce has published no corresponding legal notice, leaving Nov 10, 2026 as the only date companies can legally rely on. With 11 days left, the IEA estimates $6.5 trillion in Western EV, chip and defense output is exposed if the harsher add-on controls (0.1% value-threshold rule) snap back into force.
items.actionable: The legal gap between Washington's claimed extension and Beijing's silence is now the single biggest near-term catalyst for the rare-earth watchlist -- this week's margin-call-driven weakness in MP/Lynas/Energy Fuels is a separate, unrelated story from the structural Nov 10 setup.

items.headline: Lynas locks in price floors on over half its output as quarterly revenue jumps 55%
items.summary: Lynas Rare Earths reported average selling prices up 88% to a record A$102.1/kg in the September quarter, lifting revenue 55% to A$310.1M (~$218M), and said it has secured minimum-price agreements covering more than half of production as Western manufacturers pay premiums for non-China supply. Lynas is separately moving to acquire Meteoric Resources, developer of the world's largest known ionic-clay rare-earth resource outside China.
items.actionable: Locked-in price floors over half of output partially insulate Lynas from this week's spot-price carnage, making it the more defensive name to hold through the Nov 10 deadline inside the rare-earth watchlist relative to MP/Energy Fuels.

items.headline: Three tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz as Qatari mediators push a peace deal in Tehran
items.summary: Iran's IRGC Navy said three oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire on Oct 30 while transiting the Strait of Hormuz's IMO traffic-separation route, in what trackers called the highest monthly rate of maritime incidents since the US-Iran conflict began. Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on Oct 31 to advance a draft peace proposal, as President Trump predicted the conflict would end 'very soon,' even as US Central Command's claim that Iranian naval forces are 'incapacitated' conflicts with the ongoing attacks.
items.actionable: Escalating tanker-mining alongside active peace diplomacy keeps oil's geopolitical risk premium genuinely two-sided into next week -- it's a floor under gold's safe-haven bid even while rate-driven selling dominates the metals tape, so don't read Friday's gold dip as the geopolitical story going away.

items.headline: Oil set for fourth straight monthly gain as Hormuz risk premium holds near 13-month highs
items.summary: Brent crude traded near $117.62/bbl and WTI near $104.18/bbl on Oct 30, with Brent on track to finish October roughly 13% higher and WTI about 15% higher -- a fourth consecutive monthly gain -- driven by the Hormuz tanker-mining incidents and expectations the US could resume strikes on Iran after the midterms.
items.actionable: A fourth straight monthly crude gain confirms the Hormuz risk premium is not fading despite this week's broad asset liquidation -- a reminder that energy/geopolitical risk and the rate-driven metals selloff are two distinct, currently offsetting forces.

items.headline: Binance suffers $6.3B hack, the largest crypto theft on record, as Bitcoin sinks to ~$76,500
items.summary: Binance disclosed that roughly $6.36B in digital assets was moved across 10 blockchains within about 20 minutes in what TRM Labs says appears linked to a North Korean state-sponsored hacking group; the exchange froze withdrawals, says ~$3B has been recovered/frozen, and has pledged to cover all user losses. Bitcoin fell to around $76,500 overnight -- its lowest since mid-September -- on course for its worst October since 2014, compounding Friday's broader tech-stock selloff.
items.actionable: The Binance hack is a crypto-specific operational shock layered on top of, not a read-through from, the broader equity/metals risk-off -- it confirms Friday's risk aversion spanned both traditional and digital assets but doesn't change the thesis for the non-crypto sleeves.

items.headline: SMIC posts 29% profit jump and revenue beat on AI and Huawei chip demand
items.summary: SMIC reported Oct 31 third-quarter profit up 28.9% YoY to $191.75M (ahead of the ~$178.9M estimate) and revenue up 9.7% to $2.38B, beating its own 5-7% sequential growth guidance, as AI-driven demand and Huawei's wafer-intensive LogicFolding chip strategy (used in the new Kirin 9050 Pro/Mate 90) sustained order volumes on its mature-node lines.
items.actionable: A clean earnings beat landing right at Monday's HK open is a rare bright spot for the China/HK tech sleeve, reinforcing the SMIC domestic-substitution thesis even as broader Asia sentiment is set to open weak on Friday's Wall Street rout.

items.headline: Tencent and Alibaba in talks to invest in DeepSeek at $20B+ valuation
items.summary: The Information reported Tencent and Alibaba are negotiating to take stakes in AI lab DeepSeek, which would mark its first outside capital after years of self-funding by hedge fund High-Flyer; DeepSeek's valuation target reportedly jumped from $10B to above $20B within two days of opening the round. Tencent is said to have offered to acquire up to a 20% stake, though DeepSeek is reportedly reluctant to cede that much control.
items.actionable: Consolidating China's two largest hyperscalers behind DeepSeek is a bullish medium-term signal for Tencent's AI positioning, though it's a slow-moving structural story rather than a catalyst for Monday's open.

items.headline: Singapore banks stay pressured into Nov 5-6 Q3 results as yields hold at 4.4-4.5%
items.summary: DBS, OCBC and UOB remain well off their September highs after the early-October bond-yield-driven selloff (down 6-10% at the worst), with UOB trading around S$41.37 on Oct 30. Commentary from local research houses argues the pullback reflects valuation/yield de-rating rather than credit deterioration, noting FY26 dividend yields of roughly 4.5% (DBS), 4.4% (UOB) and 3.7% (OCBC) remain intact ahead of DBS's Nov 5 and OCBC's Nov 6 earnings.
items.actionable: With Q3 results landing Nov 5-6 and dividend yields still intact, the bank sleeve's weakness looks like a yield-driven de-rating rather than a credit problem -- a reasonable candidate for the large cash pile if Monday's open extends the pullback into the earnings dates.

items.headline: Chinese coast guard ships intrude Kinmen waters twice as Taiwan tension stays elevated
items.summary: Taiwan's military tracked seven Chinese naval vessels, one official ship and six military aircraft in a single 24-hour window through Oct 29-30, with Chinese coast guard vessels chased out of Kinmen waters in separate incidents Friday morning and afternoon. President Lai Ching-te separately warned against possible Chinese interference ahead of Taiwan's upcoming local elections, while a US commander reportedly reiterated that the threat of a PLA move before 2027 remains live.
items.actionable: Persistent, unresolved Chinese military pressure on Taiwan is a standing tail-risk for the whole HK tech sleeve (Tencent, Xiaomi, SMIC) that doesn't need a new trigger to reprice risk premia lower on any fresh escalation headline -- worth monitoring but not actionable on its own this weekend.
